text: Michael Vincent Lawler, born on September 9, 1986, is an American politician serving as the U.S. representative for New York's 17th congressional district since 2023. From 2021 to 2022, he was a Republican member of the New York State Assembly representing the 97th district in Rockland County. Lawler was born to Marie (née Fortino) and Kevin Lawler and was raised in South Salem, New York, and Suffern, New York; he is Catholic and of Irish and Italian descent. He graduated from Suffern High School and earned a Bachelor of Science degree in accounting and finance from Manhattan College in 2009, graduating as valedictorian. In October 2024, The New York Times reported resurfaced photos of Lawler wearing a Michael Jackson costume with blackface at a Manhattan College Halloween party in 2006; in response, Lawler stated the costume was a sincere homage to his musical hero, emphasizing that blackface was not part of his intent. It was also reported that in 2005, J. Randy Taraborrelli, a Michael Jackson biographer, helped get Lawler, then a high school senior, into the courtroom for Jackson's trial. He served as Rob Astorino's campaign manager in his 2014 gubernatorial run and later as an assistant to Astorino as County Executive. In 2016, Lawler served as a Republican convention delegate for Donald Trump. In 2018, he co-founded the political communications firm Checkmate Strategies. In 2020, Lawler was elected to the New York State Assembly for a two-year term, defeating Democratic incumbent Ellen Jaffee. In 2022, Lawler was the Republican nominee in New York's 17th congressional district, winning the August primary and narrowly defeating Democratic incumbent and DCCC chair Sean Patrick Maloney in the November general election. On November 5, 2024, Lawler was re-elected to the U.S. House of Representatives in the 17th congressional district, defeating Democratic nominee Mondaire Jones by 23,946 votes. The New York Times reported in September 2024 that Lawler was seen as a potential candidate for governor of New York in 2026, but in July 2025, he announced he would seek reelection to the House in 2026 instead. On January 4, 2023, Lawler criticized then-newly sworn Representative George Santos's conduct as "embarrassing and unbecoming" and "certainly a distraction," and called for Santos to resign. Lawler voted for Kevin McCarthy in the 2023 Speaker election, stating, "It's time for everybody to unify. It's time for everybody to move forward because the reality is the American people didn't elect us to fight over rules." On January 9, 2023, he voted in favor of the House rules package and delivered his first House speech supporting a bill to defund the IRS of funds allocated in the Inflation Reduction Act. He was one of five Republicans to vote against the Parents' Bill of Rights in March 2023, the only Republican not from the Freedom Caucus to do so, citing an unspecified amendment as going too far, though he co-sponsored the bill. On June 21, 2023, Lawler voted with 20 other Republicans to block the censure of Rep. Adam Schiff. On July 6, 2023, he introduced H.R.4493, the District of Columbia One Vote One Choice Act, to prohibit Washington, D.C., from adopting ranked-choice voting, with Representatives Claudia Tenney (R-NY-24) and Chuck Edwards (R-NC-11) as the only cosponsors. For much of 2023, Lawler banned television news cameras from his town hall meetings, rescinding the ban in early 2024. On October 5, 2023, he signed a letter with 15 House Republicans opposing the inclusion of the Ending Agricultural Trade Suppression (EATS) Act in the 2023 farm bill, which would have overturned state and local animal welfare laws restricting sales from animals raised in battery cages, gestation crates, and veal crates, arguing it would undermine states' rights and cede control to Chinese-owned pork producer WH Group and its subsidiary Smithfield Foods. In March 2024, Lawler was one of 10 House Republicans who signed a letter opposing the inclusion of the EATS Act in the 2024 farm bill. Lawler is a major supporter of raising the cap on the state and local tax deduction (SALT), a position that drew criticism from Marjorie Taylor Greene (R-GA) in May 2025; President Trump encouraged Republicans to pass a spending bill increasing the SALT cap to $30,000 from $10,000, and Lawler and other blue-state Republicans argued the increase was insufficient. Trump singled out Lawler in a May 2025 meeting, saying, "End it, Mike, just end it." On July 3, 2025, Lawler voted for the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. Lawler is described as a moderate Republican. In 2024, he was rated as the fourth most bipartisan member of the U.S. House during the 118th Congress by the Bipartisan Index. He is a co-sponsor of the American Families United Act, which addresses needs of mixed-status families in the U.S. immigration system. Lawler opposes abortion except in cases of rape or when the mother's life is at risk, but opposes a federal ban on abortion. In 2025, Lawler voted in favor of HR 1 of the 119th Congress. In August 2023, he signed a letter to the House Agriculture Committee opposing the EATS Act, which would have overturned state and local animal welfare laws, including California's Proposition 12. He also cosponsored the Puppy Protection Act to increase welfare standards for commercial dog breeders. In September 2024, Lawler was one of 11 House Republicans who signed a letter to Director of National Intelligence Avril Haines requesting an analysis of Chinese biotechnology and slaughter-free cultivated meat developments and recommendations to promote U.S. alternative proteins innovation. In May 2023, Lawler and Democrat Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ) introduced legislation expanding anti-boycott laws to include international governmental organizations, aiming to stop the Boycott, Divestment, and Sanctions movement in the U.S., but the bill faced heavy criticism from House Republicans and conservatives for violating First Amendment rights, leading House Republican leadership to scrap a vote in May 2025. In 2023, Lawler opposed the Metropolitan Transportation Authority's plan to implement congestion pricing in Manhattan, calling it an "outrageous cash grab," and in 2024, he asked President-elect Donald Trump to cancel the plan. Lawler voted for Trump in the 2024 Republican primary in New York and was one of six Republicans to sign a bipartisan letter pledging to respect the results of the 2024 presidential election. Lawler lives in Pearl River with his wife, Doina, born in Moldova, and their two daughters.
